Travel to Blackrock Depths and slay General Angerforge! Return to Warlord Goretooth when the task is complete.

Escort your prisoner, Grark Lorkrub, through Burning Steppes and through Blackrock Mountain to the Searing Gorge. You recall Lexlort mentioning that he would have his men waiting on the other side to take Grark into custody. You will also be required to hand over your Thorium Shackles to Lexlort.

The beta is capped at level 30 and the dungeon is made for 40 to 45. Blizzard showed how it was built at PAX Australia on October 9. Here is what they said, with what the game’s files already hold.
In the Riverglades, at Krol'dok Stronghold, a fortress on a hill at about 48.6, 26.3, in the zone’s level 42 part. The exact way in is not known yet.
See the stronghold on the world map
The Legacy challenge this dungeon counts for

Krol'dok Stronghold stands in the Riverglades, a new zone on the east coast of the Eastern Kingdoms, next to the Badlands, the Burning Steppes and Redridge Mountains. The zone is for levels 36 to 44. Alliance players fly to Farholde Keep, Horde players to Rog'mar.

The fortress sits on a hill in the zone’s level 42 part, beside Bolder'ok, with Twilight's Shroud (level 44) further on. The run goes up the hill and ends at the top: an early plan sent players up and back down, and the team changed it after playtests.
The game’s files already draw its buildings: on our world map the fortress stands at about 48.6, 26.3, against the border with the Badlands.
Nobody is meant to reach the Riverglades in the beta yet, though Blizzard said some players got there in large groups.
Krol'dok Stronghold on its hill, the last picture of the presentation. Picture: Blizzard at PAX Australia.
The in-game map of the Riverglades, as Blizzard showed it. The zone has its own page on our world map, with its places and levels from the game’s files.
The Riverglades on the in-game map, with the Badlands, the Burning Steppes and Redridge Mountains around it. Picture: Blizzard at PAX Australia.
At BlizzCon, Blizzard presented it as an enormous outdoor dungeon held by ogres who raid settlements and kidnap people (What’s Next panel, 13:28).

Blizzard wanted a dungeon that feels like the original game. Gnolls came first to mind, then ogres won. For the story the team went to Cho'gall, the two-headed ogre who leads the Twilight's Hammer since the Warcraft strategy games, so Krol'dok is a Twilight's Hammer ogre stronghold. Classic has few ogre buildings besides their mounds, so the team looked at the ogre fortresses of Blade's Edge Mountains, from The Burning Crusade.

The Riverglades are also home to the Brotherhood of the Horse, an Alliance order from the first Warcraft game’s manual. Their insignia is already on the army that crosses the bridge in Forever’s BlizzCon cinematic, while the dwarf and the bear hide.
Krol'dok Ogre Key, two keys. The second says “It get job done.”
Krol'dok Moulding, which begins a quest. The files hold two of them.
Krol'dok Battlegear, a set of five pieces Blizzard still keeps hidden: see the hidden items.

Blizzard did not name the bosses, but showed five of them: a big ogre in purple, an ogre with two axes, a green-skinned woman between two wolves, a two-headed ogre holding a purple crystal, and a heavy red ogre with one horn.
The encounter designers’ favourite part was writing the ogres’ lines. Two read at PAX: “Bigger rock, bigger stick!” and “Puny! Pathetic! You suffer now!”

On a bridge, the dungeon sends waves of enemies at you, and the bridge has a hole. A player who falls through usually lives and has to find the way back up. The team found the hole in an early playtest and kept it on purpose: “bro, they’re ogres.”
The bosses Blizzard showed, without their names. Picture: Blizzard at PAX Australia.
The hole in the bridge, framed in yellow, during a playtest. Picture: Blizzard at PAX Australia.

The beta stops below level 35, so nobody has run the dungeon outside the BlizzCon demo. What Blizzard, the game's files and the first explorers have shown so far, updated as the beta opens it.
Gillijim's Isle, in the sea southwest of Stranglethorn Vale. The portal is in Sunken Hollow, a cave on the island; explorers found it in the beta, not working yet.
The Legacy challenge this dungeon counts for

The city stands on Gillijim's Isle, in the sea southwest of Stranglethorn Vale. Blizzard made this island for the original game and removed it during the alpha, before the beta. Its name stayed on the empty sea, where Classic still shows it today, and the island still appears in the game's intro cinematic. In Forever the island is back, with a ruined troll city on it. No boat or flight path goes there yet.
On September 26, Rhysdog swam there from the Southern Savage Coast. He drowned once on the way, came back with a Soulstone, then walked the whole island. His video shows:
A troll city in ruins, with nobody in it: paved squares, wide stairs, serpent statues, troll heads, coral and braziers of blue fire.
Atal'Byzal, the part of the city under the sea: flooded halls he compares to the Sunken Temple.
A pirate ship wrecked among the ruins.
Sunken Hollow, a cave with a blue portal that does not work yet. Next to it, the game moves the chat to the channels of The Drowned City: the portal is most likely the way into the dungeon.
The ruins and the wrecked ship. Picture: Blizzard.
A giant skeleton under a rock arch. Rhysdog passes it just before the portal. Picture: Blizzard.
The portal in Sunken Hollow, the chat just moved to the channels of The Drowned City. Picture: Rhysdog.

At BlizzCon, Blizzard presented ancient troll ruins off the coast of Stranglethorn Vale, long under the waves, that have suddenly risen out of the ocean. Trolls and naga are there, and a pirate ship has crashed into the place (What's Next panel, 23:31).
Item texts in the beta give the city its old name, “I'lalai the Drowned City”, a lost troll city. Four stone tablets, quest items you can read, tell its story:
The First Tablet of I'lalaiA Fate in Blood
The Second Tablet of I'lalaiThe First Tidebearer
The Third Tablet of I'lalaiThe Cracked and Cursed
The Fourth Tablet of I'lalaiLoa of the Lost
Tale of I'lalai in Zandali, copied into modern Zandali by Kin'weelay, and

Translated Tale of I'lalai, by Loremaster Dibbs. Kin'weelay is the troll scholar at Grom'gol Base Camp who already sends players to the Vile Reef for a tablet shard in Classic (The Vile Reef). The tablets' own words are not in the beta's files yet.
Other quest items point to quests around the city:

Wowhead's Forever database has six creatures titled “Staging Area 1” to “Staging Area 6”, placeholder titles that look like the dungeon's boss slots:

Zul'Alai, in the first slot, is also the first boss players met at the BlizzCon demo: he goes into a rage near death and hits the whole group hard. Warcraft Tavern names a second boss from the demo, Zin'aka, a tank killer the database does not have.

The Legacy challenge counts the dungeon as done when creature 260274 dies, an id no database names yet. For Ruins of Lordaeron the same challenge counts Rath'mael, its last boss, so 260274 is probably the Drowned City's last boss.

On the way, the demo had makrura and small crabs first, then risen troll sentries, then naga in tight packs. The same database names Brinescale Priestess, Saltscale Muckdweller, Saltseer Manhunter, Deathless Sorcerer, Makrura Snapper, Chasm Crawler and Goaz Warder. Saltseer Manhunters drop
